transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-25
Time: 10:30 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO - Emergent AI), Sara Gomez (Head of ML), Ben Lee (Infra)

[00:00] Maria: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maria from redwood inference, this is liam our solutions eng, quick intros? 
[00:12] Ravi: hi ravi here, cto at emergent ai, thanks for setting this up
[00:16] Sara: sara, head of ml, i'll lead the eval
[00:20] Ben: ben infra, i'll be involved for networking and on prem questions
[00:25] Liam: great, quick agenda: quickstart flow, hosted vs dedicated vs private, free credits and time to first token, and then next steps / p o c scoping
[00:35] Maria: maybe start with sara, what are you trying to build and what's success look like? 
[00:42] Sara: sure, we want to add an assistant to our product for summarization and code-gen support, early stage but critical latency under 500ms token for chat flows, cost is also big - we have high qps on some endpoints so unit cost matters
[01:05] Ravi: also security - we handle PII, need SOC2 and SSO and KMS support, and potentially private deployment for certain customers
[01:20] Maria: totally, that's common. quick question on timeline - how fast do you want to get something live? 
[01:27] Sara: ideally a POC in 2-3 weeks, and if that goes well we'd move to a pilot with 1-2 models in prod in 2 months
[01:35] Maria: great, that aligns with our quickstart. liam, can you walk through the self-serve API quickstart and free credits? 
[01:42] Liam: yeah, so for plg quickstart you sign up, we allocate free credits (we usually offer a test pack, we'll provide 30k tokens or equivalent credits), there's a one-file example to get a token and call the hosted api, typical time to first token is under 5 minutes after sign-up, you can spin up a dedicated pool in a few hours for larger throughput but initial dev is hosted
[02:10] Ben: that's impressive, does the quickstart require any VPC peering or open firewall rules? we prefer not to open inbound ports
[02:18] Liam: no, hosted api is outbound only, no inbound peering required. if you choose dedicated or private, we support VPC peering and private link, in on-prem case we have an appliance package
[02:33] Sara: when you say dedicated pool in a few hours what's involved? licensing, capacity, cost? 
[02:40] Maria: dedicated is reserved capacity, there's a commit and we provision GPU pool, and you get predictable throughput and isolation. cost depends on model family and qps; liam can show typical throughput numbers vs cost in the follow-up
[02:55] Liam: to add, we have quantization profiles and batching configs to reduce unit cost by up to 3x for some workloads; but if your tail latency target is strict we tune for latency instead of max cost savings
[03:15] Ravi: security - do you have SOC2 and is there audit logging and KMS? our security team will ask for encryption at rest with customer-managed keys
[03:24] Maria: yes soc2-plus audit logs, we integrate with KMS and HSM for private deployments, for hosted we offer managed key options and can discuss bringing your own key for Private
[03:36] Sara: and SSO? we use okta
[03:40] Liam: SAML/Okta is supported for the console and role based access controls, same for dedicated and private
[03:47] Ben: curious about data retention - for hosted api do you retain prompts and outputs? we need no retention for customer data in many cases
[03:55] Maria: we have configurable retention policies; by default we don't retain user data for model training and can set zero retention for enterprise tenants on dedicated/private
[04:05] Sara: ok good. can you tell me more about time-to-first-token for embedded use cases? we saw numbers under 200ms for single token but in practice startup jitter adds
[04:15] Liam: for small seqs and cached prefices we see 50-200ms median token latency on our hosted endpoints for our optimized models, cold-start for new sessions can add 100-300ms, that's where prefix caching helps
[04:30] Ravi: for our codegen flows tokens can be long - 3k tokens per response sometimes, does the hosted api support streaming? 
[04:40] Maria: yes streaming is supported; function/tool calling and structured output too
[04:45] Sara: what about model selection - we prefer open models, do you have a catalog? 
[04:50] Liam: we maintain a model catalog of curated open models + verified performance profiles, and we can recommend quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs
[05:02] Ben: for dedicated/p rivate networking, what's the onboarding time? we can't have long lead times
[05:08] Maria: dedicated provisioning is often a day to a few hours for standard configs once contract and billing are set; private/VPC can take longer depending on network review but we have playbooks to speed it up
[05:20] Sara: for the POC we want to run a small benchmark: our prompt set (approx 200 unique prompts), run 10k queries and measure p99 latency and cost. can you support that? 
[05:32] Liam: absolutely, we can do a benchmark run on hosted or on a dedicated trial. we'll need prompt set and expected concurrency profile
[05:40] Maria: we'll also share our quickstart scripts and a benchmark spreadsheet template
[05:45] Ravi: any limitations on tokenization or special tokens? we use mixed byte encodings sometimes
[05:52] Liam: models handle utf-8; if you have edge cases we can test with your dataset
[06:00] Ben: integration with our infra - we use terraform and k8s, do you have terraform modules or helm charts for private? 
[06:08] Maria: yes we provide terraform modules for private and dedicated provisioning, and helm charts for on-prem appliance
[06:15] Sara: cost question: do you expose per-token billing in the console and breakdown by route? 
[06:22] Liam: yes cost breakdowns per-token and per-route in console; you can set quotas and rate limits per api key
[06:30] Maria: okay let's talk about next steps: we'll send a quickstart guide, grant trial credits, and book a technical deep dive to set up benchmarks
[06:40] Ravi: sounds good. can we get security docs? our legal will ask for SOC2 report and DPA
[06:45] Maria: yes we'll include SOC2, DPA, and network diagrams in the packet
[06:50] Sara: any gotchas for embeddings? we also plan to use embeddings in search and want consistent vectors across quantization
[06:58] Liam: embeddings are deterministic per model; quantization doesn't change the embedding model, but you should verify vector stability across quant variants; we can assist
[07:10] Ben: for private/on-prem do you support customer-managed KMS even offline? some customers need HSM offline key wraps
[07:20] Maria: yes for private deployments we can integrate HSM and do key wraps offline; need a security review to scope
[07:30] Sara: ok, what's a realistic POC success criteria? for us: p99 < 700ms hosted or dedicated, cost < $0.02 per 1k tokens (example), and successful SOC2 review
[07:45] Liam: that seems reasonable; we'll help set benchmarks and quantify costs per model and config
[08:00] Maria: any constraints on dataset sharing? we can sign an NDA or use secure s3 access for tests
[08:08] Ravi: we'll provide secure s3 with temp creds, prefer no long-term retention
[08:15] Maria: perfect, we'll send steps to provision credentials and the quickstart link
[08:20] Sara: can we get a short demo of the quickstart now or is that separate? 
[08:25] Liam: we can do a live quickstart but given time we can do it in the deep dive; quickstart is 3-5 minutes if you follow the script
[08:35] Maria: recap: send quickstart + SOC2 + DPA + trial credits. schedule deep dive for benchmarks. customer to share prompt set and concurrency profile. liam to own benchmark scoping
[08:50] Ravi: thanks all
[08:52] Maria: thank you, we'll follow up by EOD with links and credits

[44:30] call end

Notes: occasional minor transcription errors (names, acronyms). References: quickstart repo (link), benchmark template (link), SOC2 & DPA (link).
